A.notes: A has a strong, specific idea: the house itself becomes the interface, from the facade drawing and level-by-level room structure to the rooftop skyline and the closing arrival line. Typography is the main identity and feels unusually poised, though the long vertical spacing makes some sections feel a little under-resolved rather than pixel-tight. From the scroll frames, motion appears concept-led—the building details and rooftop sequence progress with scroll—but I cannot fully verify nuance from stills alone.

B.notes: B is clear, elegant and easy to use, with the arched door as a fitting signature tied to arrival and the house history. It is more conventional in structure and pacing, so while it is polished, it feels closer to a refined template than a singular concept carried through every section. The scroll-strip shows little meaningful progression beyond standard section changes, so motion reads minimal or generic rather than story-bearing.

raw.why: A is the more distinctive and fully authored response to the brief, turning the house, its levels and its arrival signature into the organizing idea of the whole site.
